fields.questionText:
(a) Define a universal indicator. Mention its one use.
(b) Solution 'A' gives pink colour when a drop of phenolphthalein indicator is added to it. Solution 'B' gives a red colour when a drop of methyl orange is added to it. What type of solutions are 'A' and 'B' and which of these will have higher pH?
(c) Name one salt whose solution has pH greater than 7 and one salt whose solution has pH less than 7.
fields.answer: (a) A universal indicator is a mixture of several indicators that shows different colours at different pH values; it is used to find the approximate pH (strength) of a solution. (b) 'A' is basic and 'B' is acidic; 'A' has the higher pH (more than 7). (c) pH > 7: sodium carbonate (Na2CO3); pH < 7: ammonium chloride (NH4Cl) (or copper sulphate, CuSO4).
solutionSteps: [1 mark] (a) Universal indicator is a mixture of indicators showing different colours at different pH values; use: to determine the approximate pH / strength of an acid or base.
[1 mark] (b) Phenolphthalein turns pink in a base, so 'A' is basic; methyl orange turns red in an acid, so 'B' is acidic; hence 'A' has the higher pH (> 7).
[1 mark] (c) Na2CO3 (salt of strong base + weak acid) gives pH > 7; NH4Cl (salt of strong acid + weak base) gives pH < 7.
fields.finalAnswer: (a) Mixture of indicators; finds pH. (b) A basic, B acidic; A has higher pH. (c) Na2CO3 (pH > 7); NH4Cl (pH < 7).

rationale: Removed page header from part (c); completed truncated answer and the 'pH is more than,' gap; split into 3 x [1 mark] steps.

fields.questionText:
In the chlor-alkali process, electrolysis of brine gives gas 'X' (chlorine) at the anode and gas 'Y' (hydrogen) at the cathode.
(i) Write a balanced chemical equation for the reaction that takes place when 'X' and 'Y' react with each other.
(ii) The product so formed turns blue litmus red only when it is wet, not when dry. Why?
fields.answer: (i) H2 + Cl2 → 2HCl. (ii) Dry HCl gas does not release H+ ions; only in the presence of water does it ionise (HCl + H2O → H3O+ + Cl−), and these H+ ions turn blue litmus red.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] (i) H2(g) + Cl2(g) → 2HCl(g).
[1 mark] (ii) HCl shows acidic behaviour only in water: HCl + H2O → H3O+ + Cl−; dry HCl gives no H+ ions, so only wet HCl turns blue litmus red.
fields.finalAnswer: (i) H2 + Cl2 → 2HCl; (ii) H+ (H3O+) ions form only in the presence of water.

rationale: Not a real case (no sub-parts, context missing, CBSE-sourced): made the stem self-contained with (i)/(ii) and re-tagged to its true size — Section B, 2-mark Short; steps re-marked 1+1.

fields.questionText:
pH is measured using a pH meter, which comprises a detecting unit consisting of a pH sensitive glass electrode and an indicating unit which displays the pH reading on a screen.

To measure the pH of a solution, the glass electrode is dipped into the solution and the pH is displayed on the screen of the indicating unit. Before measuring the pH of another solution, the glass electrode is rinsed with distilled water and dried carefully with tissue paper.

How is the pH reading of the second solution likely to be affected if the glass electrode is not dried with tissue paper in the following cases?
(i) if the second solution being measured is acidic in nature
(ii) if the second solution being measured is basic in nature
solutionSteps: [1 mark] (i) Water left on the electrode dilutes the acidic solution, lowering its H+ ion concentration, so the meter shows a slightly higher pH than the actual value.
[1 mark] (ii) Water left on the electrode dilutes the basic solution, lowering its OH− ion concentration, so the meter shows a slightly lower pH than the actual value.

rationale: Photo of the pH meter is decorative, not needed to answer; replaced 'as shown below' with a words description; added the dilution reason to steps; answer unchanged.

solutionSteps: [1 mark] (a) P (pH 2) is strongly acidic and S (pH 13) is strongly basic — lower pH means more H+ ions, higher pH more OH− ions.
[1 mark] (b) Q (pH 7) is neutral.
[1 mark] (c) Mixing the strong acid P with the strong base S causes a neutralisation reaction.
[1 mark] (c) Products are a salt and water, e.g. HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H2O.
fields.finalAnswer: (a) P strongly acidic, S strongly basic; (b) Q neutral; (c) neutralisation — salt + water.
fields.explanation: pH < 7 is acidic (the lower, the stronger), pH 7 is neutral and pH > 7 is basic (the higher, the stronger). An acid and a base react to form salt and water (neutralisation).
